task: Measure selected-test Fast Debug checker work for the Phase 26.1.1 X0 fixture.
observation: Filtering `moss test --interp <file> <filter>` selected the requested test for execution but still produced checker identities for all eight app and dependency functions in the two-package fixture. The reached test's target set contains three functions; the app-only test's target set contains one.
impact: The command result alone did not expose the checker scope, so the package-perf harness needed compiler profile identities to show that execution filtering is not yet entry-scoped checking. R11 remains unimplemented.
evidence: MOSS_M1_ENFORCE_TARGETS=1 make package-perf fails with 8 observed identities versus the 3-function `baseline_reach` target

resolution.summary: Keep as the X0 baseline; entry-scoped checking is part of X2 after the X1 ABI decision.

task: Repair Phase 26.1.1 Fast Debug reachability and scoped checking.
observation: A reached handler replying with an inferred nominal state value failed Fast Debug with TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED even though moss check accepted it. The state initializer was the only reference to the nominal type, so pruning unrelated callable bodies also removed the declaration identity needed for reply inference.
impact: The issue was reproduced with tests/tooling/fixtures/builtin_generic_typing/underscore_domain_state.moss and fixed by retaining nominal declarations referenced from selected object/domain state initializers. The complete builtin typing fixture set then passed: 129 probes, zero failures.
evidence: Before fix, build/compiler/moss-opt run --interp on that fixture returned TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED for payload.value

resolution.summary: Preserve declaration identities referenced by reached inferred state initializers. Focused gates confirm the fix; the full uninterrupted make check remains pending.

task: Complete ABI-v10 Section 1 generic dependency bodies and Fast Debug reachability.
observation: A private generic helper reachable from exported concrete SDK functions was present in the ABI-v10 Section 1 dependency record but the reader skipped its generic_stmt records. Fast Debug entered text__matches_at and returned unit, causing the SDK replacement edge test to leave its input unchanged.
impact: The v10 reader now retains generic_stmt and generic_source for private generic dependency records while still skipping legacy body lines for exported callables that use checked-body records. The SDK Fast Debug acceptance tests pass 3/3.
evidence: make --jobs="$(nproc)" check at b7a7890d: sdk_text_encoding failed; full run completed 142/148
MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 MOSS=<repo>/build/compiler/moss-opt margo debug --trace showed text__matches_at returning unit before the fix
MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 MOSS=<repo>/build/compiler/moss-opt margo test --interp in sdk/text-encoding-acceptance: 3 passed

resolution.summary: Keep digest-covered private generic dependency bodies available to scoped checking and execution without expanding ABI-v10 checked-body coverage.

task: Keep dependency source locations out of Section 1 identity while preserving xref and diagnostic locations.
observation: A dependency blank-line edit moves generic body and provenance line numbers. Hashing emitted Section 1 bytes directly caused unchanged consumers to recheck. Normalizing only the consumer-facing Section 1 fields preserves the dependency's absolute metadata while leaving its consumers cached.
impact: ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 now normalize source-position fields for interface identity. The X1 gates verify that a dependency blank-line edit checks only the provider, changes its sidecar and Section 2, and preserves the Section 1 digest; Emacs xref resolves the moved declaration at line 65.

resolution.summary: Normalize source positions in Section 1 digest and consumer fingerprint inputs; retain absolute lines in the provider artifact and navigation sidecar.
